17# gcu400 tuning (2026-11-13, L600, bench kernel mode do_bench median 

18# w1000/r100, core shapes 512^3..4096^3): 

19# - the generic host upcast every fp16/bf16 call to fp32 (3 aten _to_copy 

20# kernels) before the mm kernels and cast the results back (2 more), and 

21# materialised both operand transposes via .contiguous() (2 aten copy 

22# kernels). At 4096^3 fp16 that path measured 4663us; the fp32 GEMM pair 

23# alone is 4395us of it. 

24# - the Triton mm kernel takes strides (NT layout flows straight into the 

25# kernel: no transpose copy), and it accumulates in fp32 

26# (dot_out_dtype=tl.float32), so skipping the host upcast is 

27# precision-neutral for the 2-D path: fp16 products are exact in fp32 and 

28# the single output rounding is the same one the upcast path performs. 

29# - saturated 2-D GEMMs (>= 2^29 MACs, the same line gcu400 bmm uses for 

30# its own native delegation) run on the captured native primo++ pipeline 

31# via the batch-1 bmm entry, which accepts the NT/transposed views with 

32# zero copies; below the line the Triton mm kernel is faster 

33# (launch-bound segment). 

34# Measured (2 GEMMs, us @ 512^3/1024^3/2048^3/4096^3): 

35# fp16 128.4/148.0/698.5/4662.9 -> 15.0/40.8/134.1/948.2 

36# fp32 34.4/122.8/636.0/4496.8 -> 26.5/80.4/448.9/3585.8 

37# The batched path keeps the generic fp32-upcast semantics (broadcast 

38# reductions in fp16 lose precision; no measured workload pays for the risk). 

39import logging 

40 

41import torch 

42 

43from .sum import sum_dim 

44 

45logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

46 

47# 2-D GEMMs at or above this many multiply-accumulates saturate the device 

48# and run faster on the native pipeline (mirror of bmm's dispatch line). 

49_2D_NATIVE_DELEGATE_WORK = 1 << 29 

50 

51 

52def _lookup_matmul_entries(): 

53 """The mm / bmm entries off the flag_gems namespace, resolved at call time. 

54 

55 Why: a backend may override mm with a kernel whose tune configs carry keys 

56 the general kernel does not declare -- kunlunxin's mm takes SPLIT_K and the 

57 general one does not -- so importing flag_gems.ops.mm directly binds the 

58 general kernel and the backend's own configs then fail with 

59 "Keyword argument SPLIT_K was specified but unrecognised". Same reasoning 

60 as _matmul() in linalg_matrix_power.py. 

61 

62 Returns: 

63 The (mm, bmm) callables for the active backend. 

64 """ 

65 from flag_gems import bmm, mm 

66 

67 return mm, bmm 

68 

69 

70def _matmul_2d_or_batched(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: 

71 """Matrix multiply using the Triton mm/bmm kernels. 

72 

73 Both ``a`` and ``b`` have their contracting dimension as the last two 

74 dims (``(..., M, K)`` and ``(..., K, N)``). Leading batch dimensions are 

75 broadcast against each other, mirroring ``torch.matmul``. 

76 """ 

77 if a.dim() == 2 and b.dim() == 2: 

78 mm, bmm = _lookup_matmul_entries() 

79 M, K = a.shape 

80 N = b.shape[1] 

81 if M * N * K >= _2D_NATIVE_DELEGATE_WORK: 

82 # Batch-1 views: bmm routes saturated GEMMs to the captured 

83 # native kernel, which takes arbitrary strides (the NT operand 

84 # views need no transpose-copy materialisation). 

85 return bmm(a.unsqueeze(0), b.unsqueeze(0)).squeeze(0) 

86 # Strides (including NT transposed views) flow straight into the 

87 # Triton kernel; do not materialise transposes with .contiguous(). 

88 return mm(a, b) 

89 

90 M, K = a.shape[-2], a.shape[-1] 

91 K2, N = b.shape[-2], b.shape[-1] 

92 batch_shape = torch.broadcast_shapes(a.shape[:-2], b.shape[:-2]) 

93 

94 a_exp = a.expand(*batch_shape, M, K).reshape(-1, M, K).contiguous() 

95 b_exp = b.expand(*batch_shape, K2, N).reshape(-1, K2, N).contiguous() 

96 _, bmm = _lookup_matmul_entries() 

97 out = bmm(a_exp, b_exp) 

98 return out.reshape(*batch_shape, M, N) 

99

101def _sum_to(grad: torch.Tensor, shape) -> torch.Tensor: 

102 """Reduce ``grad`` (a broadcasted gradient) back to ``shape`` via summation.""" 

103 shape = tuple(shape) 

104 while grad.dim() > len(shape): 

105 grad = sum_dim(grad, dim=[0], keepdim=False) 

106 for i in range(len(shape)): 

107 if shape[i] == 1 and grad.shape[i] != 1: 

108 grad = sum_dim(grad, dim=[i], keepdim=True) 

109 return grad 

110 

111 

112def matmul_backward( 

113 grad: torch.Tensor, 

114 self: torch.Tensor, 

115 other: torch.Tensor, 

116 mask, 

117): 

118 """Backward pass for ``torch.matmul``. 

119 

120 Given ``out = matmul(self, other)`` and the upstream gradient ``grad``, 

121 returns ``(grad_self, grad_other)``. Each is ``None`` when the 

122 corresponding entry of ``mask`` is False. 

123 """ 

124 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 MATMUL_BACKWARD") 

125 

126 need_self, need_other = bool(mask[0]), bool(mask[1]) 

127 

128 dim_self = self.dim() 

129 dim_other = other.dim() 

130 

131 # 2-D x 2-D (1-D operands fold up to 2-D) takes the fast path: the Triton 

132 # mm / native kernels accumulate in fp32, so fp16/bf16 inputs keep full 

133 # accumulation precision without any host upcast. The batched path below 

134 # still chains broadcast reductions, where fp16/bf16 partial sums lose 

135 # precision, so it keeps the fp32-upcast semantics. 

136 two_d = dim_self <= 2 and dim_other <= 2 

137 

138 compute_dtype = self.dtype 

139 if not two_d and self.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16): 

140 compute_dtype = torch.float32 

141 

142 s = self.to(compute_dtype) if self.dtype != compute_dtype else self 

143 o = other.to(compute_dtype) if other.dtype != compute_dtype else other 

144 g = grad.to(compute_dtype) if grad.dtype != compute_dtype else grad 

145 

146 # Fold 1D operands up to 2D, mirroring how torch.matmul treats vectors: 

147 # a 1D `self` becomes (1, K) and a 1D `other` becomes (K, 1). The folded 

148 # dimensions are dropped from the forward output, so they must be inserted 

149 # back into `grad` before computing the gradients. 

150 folded_self = dim_self == 1 

151 folded_other = dim_other == 1 

152 

153 if folded_self: 

154 s = s.unsqueeze(-2) 

155 if folded_other: 

156 o = o.unsqueeze(-1) 

157 

158 if folded_other: 

159 g = g.unsqueeze(-1) 

160 if folded_self: 

161 g = g.unsqueeze(-2) 

162 

163 grad_self = None 

164 grad_other = None 

165 

166 if need_self: 

167 # grad_self = grad @ other^T 

168 gs = _matmul_2d_or_batched(g, o.transpose(-2, -1)) 

169 gs = _sum_to(gs, s.shape) 

170 if folded_self: 

171 gs = gs.squeeze(-2) 

172 grad_self = gs.to(self.dtype) if gs.dtype != self.dtype else gs 

173 

174 if need_other: 

175 # grad_other = self^T @ grad 

176 go = _matmul_2d_or_batched(s.transpose(-2, -1), g) 

177 go = _sum_to(go, o.shape) 

178 if folded_other: 

179 go = go.squeeze(-1) 

180 grad_other = go.to(other.dtype) if go.dtype != other.dtype else go 

181 

182 return grad_self, grad_other
